main_text.l: Epodus 2.versuum 15.
QVid post mortem Coronidis confecutum sit: quo-
modo exemptus Æsculapius & Chironi erudiendus
sit traditus.
Ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τείχει[?].) Consequentia mortis sunt sepultura, ro-
gus apud veteres. τεῖχος ξύλινον vocat πυρκαϊὰν[?], rogum. sic
σέλας Ἀφαίστου ignis ardentis periphrasis.
Τὸν ἔειπεν Ἀπόλλων[?].) Alterum ἐπιμύρον[?], commiseratio pa-
terna, & quomodo Æsculapium ex flammis eripuerit.
Οὔνεκα [illegible, ~8 letters].) μίμησις patris condolentis affectum ex-
primens: sic Ovidius.

l.i: Non tulit in cineres labi sua Phœbus eosdem
Semina: sed natum flammis uteroque parentis

main_text.l: Βάμματι δ' ἐν πρώτῳ[?].) Seruatur Æsculapius ex igni: mirum
autem facit Apollinem vno βήματι[?] ex Pythone urbe in
Laceria transiisse. Aristarchus hic legit τετράτῳ[?], quòd tres
passus fecerit.
Καὶ ῥά μιν[?].) Duo praecipuè hactenus de Æsculapio do-
cuit, genus maternum, cuius occasione fatum & calami-
tates matris exposuit: alterum nativitatem mirabilem
Æsculapij, mortua matre ex utero & flammis eripitur.
Tertio iam docet, quis illi datus praeceptor, Centaurus
Magnesius, hoc est, Chiron Thessalus: sic Ovid.

l.i: Eripuit geminiq; tulit Chironis in antrum.

main_text.l: recte autem νόσις vocat πολυπήμονας[?], h.e. πολλῶν τῶν πημάτων[?].
Strophe 3.versuum 13.
QVantus professione effectus fuerit Æsculapius, quos
morbos curarit, & quomodo curarit, hæc Strophe
edocet.
Τῆς μὲν ὧν[?].) Quartus locus de professione medica, in qua
quantus extiterit Aesculapius docet: quatuor praecipua
recenset morborum genera: αὐτόφυτα ἕλκη, innata vlcera,
vt cancer: secundo τραύματα quae ferro fiunt: tertio, βολὴ
iactus, vt lapide, fuste, plaga incussa: quarto καύσεις, vt fe-
brium

page.notes: Several Greek words are uncertain because the scan is faint and small; they are marked [?]. The Greek line after "Οὔνεκα" could not be read letter by letter and is marked illegible. The running text ends mid-word ("fe-brium") at the foot of the page, so the paragraph continues on the next page. Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout (e.g. "eosdem", "sed", "sua"), and u/v is normalised as specified; printed spellings such as "Thessalus" and "Ovidius" are otherwise kept as printed. The opening verse block is treated as the continuation of a stanza from the previous page.
